fields.description: What kind of entry this is, in a closed vocabulary this app owns rather than a society's. It is display only: the deployment's own status is the state machine, and nothing in the code branches on this value. It exists so a feed reads as an account of what happened rather than a column of undifferentiated notes. `status` and `roster` are written by the service when a deployment moves or somebody joins or leaves, which is what makes the feed a timeline instead of only the notes people remembered to write.
fields.label: Entry

fields.description: Who wrote it. The login, taken from the session at the moment the entry was written and never passed in by a caller, so a feed cannot be made to say somebody said something they did not.
fields.label: Author

fields.description: When it was written. Stamped by the service, not by the form, so the order of a feed is the order things happened in.
fields.label: Posted On

fields.description: What was said, in the author's own words. Plain text, and rendered as a string wherever it is shown, for the same reason a task update's note is plain: writing on a record somebody else will open is not permission to run markup in their browser.
fields.label: Note

fields.description: A photograph attached to this entry — the site on arrival, the distribution under way, the damage being reported. One image per entry rather than a gallery on the deployment: a photograph belongs to the moment it was taken, and a second one is a second entry with its own note and its own time.
fields.label: Attachment
